glance_takeaway: The page is a research write-up titled 'murmur' about teaching a small CNN classifier to recognize bird calls using cheap, reverberation-inspired audio augmentations. The main message, from the bold lead paragraph, is that the bet is 'partially supported': cheap reverb augmentation lifts validation macro-F1 from 0.612 to 0.671 (+5.9 points) at negligible compute, but the gain concentrates in common classes and barely reaches the rare tail. The lede also flags that not every augmentation helped (pitch/time-stretch regressed, noise-mixing was null), the best result is a stack of tricks, and the next step is class-conditional augmentation.

F1.note: Lede + 'The bet' blockquote + H1/H2 split state the reverb-augmentation hypothesis and the efficiency-vs-bigger-architecture half.

F2.note: The dataset: '6,200 clips across 34 species, 5 s mono at 32 kHz, featurised as 128-mel log-mel spectrograms (25 ms window / 10 ms hop)'.

F3.note: '70/15/15 train/val/test, stratified by species and seeded - roughly 930 clips each for validation and the held-out test set'.

F4.note: '8 most common species account for ~52%'; American Robin 480; '11 species have fewer than 80 clips ... and 5 have fewer than 45'; 'Median clips per class ~120'.

F5.note: Metric is validation macro-F1 weighting tail equally (blockquote); 'Seed-to-seed variability ... ~ +/-0.006'.

F6.note: Ledger table row 01 baseline-clean 0.612 'floor'; exp-01 section repeats.

F8.note: Row 03 pitchshift-timestretch 0.589, marked regression below baseline; exp-03 callout '-0.023 vs baseline'.

F9.note: Row 04 noise-mix-snr 0.643, note 'null vs exp-02'; exp-04 callout '+0.002 vs exp-02'.

F10.note: Row 05 stack-reverb-noise-specaug 0.671 (+0.059) 'best', bolded best row + Current best callout.

F11.note: Row 06 reverb-heavy-longrt60 0.663 below best; exp-06 section: helps common, hurts rare, class-dependent.

F12.note: exp-03 callout + post-mortem: pitch/time warping smears fine spectral/timing cues, <50 real clips, common classes unaffected.

F13.note: exp-04 callout: +0.002 inside +/-0.006 seed noise = null; kept because it composes with SpecAugment in exp-05.

F14.note: Reproduce-recipe code block lists small_cnn, logmel_128, reverb p0.5 rt60 0.3-0.6, noise 5-20 dB, SpecAugment 2/2, class_balanced 0.5; pitch/stretch and heavy reverb OFF.

F15.note: Per-species table exp-01->exp-05: Robin 0.79->0.85, Cardinal 0.76->0.83, Song Sparrow 0.68->0.74, Wood Thrush 0.51->0.54, Kirtland's 0.34->0.33; text '~4.5 of the 5.9 points come from common/mid'.

strengths: Exceptionally faithful: every one of the 15 ground-truth facts is present and numerically exact, with no distortion or overselling.
Scrupulous caveat discipline - explicit 'honest caveat' notes, null-result framing, '±0.006 seed noise', 'asserted not shown' for H2, and a held-out-test-untouched discipline note.
The bold summary lede front-loads the headline verdict (T1) so it lands even on a quick scan.
Clear section hierarchy, semantic color-coded ledger deltas and good/bad/flat callouts, and an actual reproduce recipe give a motivated reader near-complete depth.
weaknesses: Pure prose baseline: the glance is a dense text block, so takeaways T2/T3/T4 (regression, stack, class-conditional next step) require reading a running paragraph rather than landing visually.
The brief explicitly wanted the metric trajectory made legible; it is delivered as a table, with no chart of the baseline->best arc that 'is the result'.
Long single-column scroll with no in-page navigation/anchors, so re-finding a specific item means scrolling.
Visual encoding does minimal work beyond typography and a few colored table cells - little that a text dump could not achieve.
